subject: E2E latency SLO discovery — p95/p99 targets, throughput & streaming follow-ups
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@veridian.ai>, Veridian SRE <sre@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:15:00 +0000
Subject: E2E latency SLO discovery — p95/p99 targets, throughput & streaming follow-ups

Thanks again for the sync today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on measurements and test windows. High level takeaways:

- Veridian cares about end-to-end (client -> Redwood hosted -> model -> client) p95/p99 for the production inference path. Primary target bands discussed: p95 ~ 120-200ms and p99 ~ 300-500ms depending on prompt size and streaming vs non-streaming.
- You currently observe spikes in p99 under bursty traffic that coincide with concurrent KV cache misses and long tail model warmup.
- Throughput and sustained QPS expectations: preliminary ask is ~80 QPS sustained with bursts to 250 QPS for short windows. Concurrent in-flight requests estimated at ~120 active connections for chat streaming flows.

Action items (proposed):
1) Veridian: share representative traffic profile (token distributions, typical prompt/response lengths, streaming vs blocking split). See request below for format.
2) Redwood: provide an SLO test plan (end-to-end harness that measures p95/p99 by client envelope including network time) and a demo slot where we run a 2-hour soak with production-shaped traffic.
3) Joint: agree measurement methodology (client-side timing capture, definition of warm vs steady state, how we count retries and partial streams).

Measurement clarifications we need from you to size the PoC:
- Typical request token counts (prompt, expected response) percentiles (p50/p90/p99).
- Ratio of streaming responses (token-by-token) vs full-response buffering.
- Acceptable cutoffs for p95/p99 per endpoint (e.g., chat vs single-shot completion).
- Any required regional egress constraints or throughput shaping windows.

Next proposed dates: Redwood can run the soak test Thu 17 Jun 14:00-16:00 PT or Fri 18 Jun 09:00-11:00 PT (please confirm preferred). We will attach a draft test plan and the runbook.

Attachments included with this thread: veridian_traffic_profile.json (sample traffic shape), redwood_slo_test_plan.xlsx (draft test cases), rdw-demo-runbook.md (demo checklist).

Happy to sync on a short call if you want to walk the plan line-by-line.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@veridian.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Veridian SRE <sre@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 01:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: E2E latency SLO discovery — p95/p99 targets, throughput & streaming follow-ups

Thanks Jordan — appreciated the summary. Quick answers and attached traffic snapshot.

- We attached veridian_traffic_profile.json showing our token percentiles for the last 30 days. Short summary: prompt p50=18 tokens, p90=68, p99=220. Response p50=64 tokens, p90=320, p99=950.
- Streaming is dominant for chat flows (approx 65% of calls). For single-shot completions (search summarization) we buffer responses.
- Peak sustained QPS during business hours ~80, typical bursts to 200–300 for short campaigns. Concurrent websocket connections we see ~80-140 depending on campaign traffic.
- Target SLOs we need: per-chat p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms for 95% of endpoints; single-shot endpoints can tolerate slightly higher p99 (<=600ms) if throughput is preserved.

We'll note that our current provider reports lower median but has a long p99 tail during bursts which is causing customer issues — we're testing alternatives.

Attachment: [Attachment: veridian_traffic_profile.json (application/json)]

— Lisa Park
Director, Platform Reliability | Veridian
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@veridian.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: E2E latency SLO discovery — test plan + measurement details

Appreciate the data, Lisa — that's very helpful. I took a pass at the SLO test plan and sketched the measurement methodology in the spreadsheet (redwood_slo_test_plan.xlsx). Highlights and clarifications:

- Measurement definition: client-side envelope timing (TCP connect + TLS + request send + first-byte + last-byte). We will report p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and end-to-end total. For streaming we will report time-to-first-token and time-to-80%-of-tokens to capture progressive delivery.
- Warm vs steady: 20-minute ramp, then 60-minute steady window for stable stats; we'll also report warmup percentiles separately.
- Traffic shaping: Redwood harness can replay your supplied distribution (veridian_traffic_profile.json). We will run with offered concurrency shapes: sustained 80 QPS and a scheduled burst to 250 QPS for 10 minutes. We will run multiple iterations to capture variance.
- Model variants: we will test two hosted variants (quantized v1 and fp16 v2) and measure p95/p99 delta. We'll also test with and without KV prefix caching to quantify impact on p99.
- Observability: we'll provide per-request trace IDs and a CSV with timestamps for each phase (connect, first-byte, last-byte) plus server-side kernel latency samples where available.

Proposed soak windows: Thu 17 Jun 14:00-16:00 PT (primary) and Fri 18 Jun 09:00-11:00 PT (backup). Please confirm which works for you.

Attachment referenced: [Attachment: redwood_slo_test_plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

If you want, Marissa and I can run a pre-check on Wed morning to validate the harness with a 30-minute smoke.

— Ben Carter
Solutions Performance Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: E2E latency SLO discovery — scheduling and runbook

Thanks all — we’ll take Thu 17 Jun 14:00-16:00 PT for the primary soak window. Quick logistics:

- Demo/runbook: we'll follow rdw-demo-runbook.md. Please ensure any firewall IP allowlist changes are in place by Thu 12:00 PT.
- Dataset and tokens: thanks Lisa for the profile. Please confirm if there are any PII constraints — we will only replay anonymized prompts.
- Test acceptance: we will produce a post-run report with p95/p99, tail reduction analysis, and actionable recommendations (batching, cache hints, model variant suggestion). If the p99 tail is above your thresholds we will propose mitigations with estimated cost impact.

See you on the call — I'll drop calendar invites and link the runbook.

Attachment referenced: [Attachment: rdw-demo-runbook.md (text/markdown)]

— Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Reliability | Redwood Inference
